first_impression.reaction: Googled 'honeymoon planning service' while our wedding planner comparison is still open in a spreadsheet. The intro's second sentence is the right one: 'The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.' That's a standard I can hold people to, so I kept going. Went straight to the FAQ and the 'Questions to ask' list. The list is solid and, this time, it actually asks about commission. The FAQ on cost gives me nothing though, not even a typical range. No hype, no 'award-winning', which helps. But unlike most honest guides, it never says when I might not need a planner at all.

journey.quote: The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.
journey.reaction: Good. A concrete test, not a promise. I'll hold them to it.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: You describe the shape of it: how long you have, the kind of places that make you both exhale, the one thing you will not go without.
journey.reaction: 'Make you both exhale' is brochure talk. Harmless, but it's the kind of line I skim past.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: You give up none of your rights by handing the trip to someone else.
journey.reaction: Sourced and honest. It doesn't pretend I'm safer with them, just that I'm not worse off.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: Where a planner earns their place is time.
journey.reaction: Honest framing: the value is hours saved, not magic access. But the page never tells me when that time saving isn't worth paying for. A simple one-stay trip for two? I'd book that myself.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
journey.reaction: I know I'll get the fee in writing. I still don't know what it is or how it's charged. Noted for the enquiry, not a surprise on a blog.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Travel can be planned anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Big claim, nothing behind it. Planned by whom, with what local contacts? I'd check this against reviews.

journey.section: Planning the honeymoon alongside your wedding
journey.quote: Planning them as two separate projects means two sets of contacts, two sets of deadlines and two lots of quotes in foreign currencies to convert at the kitchen table.
journey.reaction: Fair point and it's the actual reason I'd consider bundling. Also the obvious upsell from wedding to honeymoon, but at least it's argued, not asserted.

journey.quote: Born in Australia and married overseas? You will always need a name change certificate for your passport.
journey.reaction: Useful, specific, and the sort of thing that actually catches people out. Didn't expect it on a sales page.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: These are worth asking whoever you speak to, including us.
journey.reaction: Holding themselves to their own checklist. That's what I want to see.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: Ask whether the rate is guaranteed, what fees or margin apply and whether the receiver pays anything at the other end.
journey.reaction: Exactly the question about where margin hides in an AUD quote. Sourced to Moneysmart. Good.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: Do you receive commission from suppliers?
journey.reaction: My first question, and it's on the list. Good.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: A straightforward question deserves a straightforward answer, and it tells you how the planner is paid on top of any fee.
journey.reaction: Asks me to demand a straight answer while the page doesn't give its own. I accept that's for the enquiry, but it's also missing the useful follow-up: will they disclose the commission amount, and does it change which hotels they recommend?

journey.quote: A fee only means something next to what it covers. Ask for the fee in writing, before any work begins, along with the inclusions, and compare planners on both.
journey.reaction: This is a dodge. I asked how much it costs and got 'ask'. Not even how planners typically charge (flat, percentage, per booking) so I know what I'm comparing.

journey.quote: Work back from your dates rather than a rule.
journey.reaction: No number at all. I'd take a sourced rough range over this.

journey.quote: With one Wedded Advisor from the first conversation to the flight home, the fee agreed in writing before any work begins and the inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit, it can be.
journey.reaction: Consistent with the rest of the page, and the CTA comes after the checklist, not before. Fine.

unanswered_questions: How do honeymoon planners typically charge (flat fee, percentage, per booking), so I know what I'm comparing across quotes?
When is a planner not worth it for a honeymoon, e.g. a single-stay trip for two?
Roughly how far ahead do couples need to book honeymoon flights and stays in peak season?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee charged and what is it? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland take commission from the hotels and suppliers it books, and will it disclose it? (deferred business detail)
Who is actually on the ground if something goes wrong mid-trip? (deferred business detail)
Can I see a real honeymoon you've planned with the actual cost? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: A fee only means something next to what it covers. Ask for the fee in writing, before any work begins, along with the inclusions, and compare planners on both.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ I read first answers 'how much' with 'ask'. Even a generic explanation of how planners charge would make it a real answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: Travel can be planned anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: Sweeping claim with nothing supporting it, on a page that otherwise sources its statements.

turn_offs_found.quote: the kind of places that make you both exhale
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional brochure language. Mild, but it's what I read as marketing.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the 'Questions to ask any planner before you agree' list, added to our planner comparison spreadsheet
Anyone marrying overseas, the 'The name on your tickets' section, because the name change certificate point catches people out

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [speak with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planning-service&utm_content=closing) and tell us anything.
cta_reaction.why: The page is honest and gives me the right questions, including commission. They go in the spreadsheet. But I'd only enquire by sending those seven questions and waiting for written answers. The page alone doesn't tell me what the fee is or whether they take a cut, so I wouldn't enquire off it yet.

top_3_changes: Make the FAQ 'How much does a honeymoon planner cost?' answer useful without stating Wedded Wonderland's fee: explain the common ways planners charge (flat fee, percentage, per booking, commission only) so readers know what to compare, sourced if possible. Currently: 'A fee only means something next to what it covers.'
Add one honest line on when a planner isn't worth it (e.g. a single stay, one currency, flexible dates), next to 'Where a planner earns their place is time.'

Extend question 7 ('Do you receive commission from suppliers?') with a generic follow-up: will they disclose the amount, and does it affect which suppliers they recommend. This is reader advice, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and questions list first, looked for catches, flagged unsupported and emotional claims
No invented brand facts; fee, commissions, on-ground team and real-honeymoon questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Deferred business details (fee basis, commissions, on-ground team, scale proof, real honeymoons, perks, Wedded Privileges) not penalised in scores or top changes

open_questions.question: Does the source pack support a generic, sourced explanation of how honeymoon planners or travel agents typically charge (flat fee, percentage, commission), and a sourced booking lead-time range for the 'How far ahead' FAQ?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'honeymoon planning service' while comparing planners for the wedding, so relevance is 4 and enquiry likelihood is 2.
Deferred business details are not penalised; suggested changes are generic reader advice requiring no Wedded Wonderland facts.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, the questions list, the 'How it works' section and the closing, with a skim of the remaining sections.
